issues.detail: Example 2 describes the todo create/delete flow in prose and refers back to earlier sections instead of giving complete runnable code, and the delete mutation is never shown.

scenarios.name: polling-dashboard-with-conditional-key
scenarios.rationale: B uses useSWR with a null key when userId is missing, a fetcher that checks res.ok and throws an ApiError carrying the status, and calls the hook unconditionally. A hand-rolls fetch in useEffect and only mentions SWR-like libraries as an aside, so it misses the useSWR requirement even though its null handling and error handling are sound.

scenarios.name: optimistic-todo-add-with-rollback
scenarios.rationale: B makes useSWRMutation its main approach, sharing the '/api/todos' key with useSWR, and passes optimisticData, populateCache and rollbackOnError: true, which matches the rubric. A's main example uses plain mutate with an async function that returns the new array, which the rubric allows. A's useSWRMutation version is only a short secondary snippet, and it doesn't show the shared useSWR key there.

scenarios.name: infinite-scroll-feed-load-more
scenarios.rationale: Response A uses useSWRInfinite from swr/infinite with a getKey(index, previous) that returns null when hasMore is false, builds page = index + 1, flattens with flatMap, and calls setSize(size + 1), so it meets every rubric item; Response B is a hand-rolled fetch/useState hook with none of the required SWR pieces.
